'the un-packaged send-off' (chunk 6, line 47) resolves via the enclosing module's Prework ('Walk in with your un-packaged session'), which per rule 1's module-signposting clause counts as prior context since Prework sits before this lecture's include-link in `learn-from-the-test.md` deck order (confirmed by reading the module file). Per-chunk count: chunk 1=1, chunk 2=2, chunk 3=1, chunk 4=1, chunk 5=1, chunk 6=1, chunk 7=1 -- at or under the <=1-per-slide budget except chunk 2's two, which fits the rule's own 'a law/consolidation slide may carry one handle per law' exception (chunk 2 names two of the three-pattern's three pieces, one handle each). Closest call, held as PASS but flagged for the maintainer: lines 13 and 41 bold a full six-word clause ('A check is a position fix' / 'A prediction is not a measurement.') rather than a <=5-word sub-span, which is literally over the rule's stated handle-length cap even though the per-slide count is within budget. Both are the file's own coined maxims (line 13's law is named in the backing block's Frameworks ledger as 'Dead reckoning and the position fix'; line 41's phrasing is one of the two lines the backing block flags as Antti-blessed, deliberate wording), and this exact pattern was reviewed by the prior instance on the pre-hooks-extraction body and not filed as REVISE for the same reason (sole coined law/principle, not incidental sentence emphasis). Held to that precedent rather than re-litigating; surfaced as a todo, not a finding.

rules_evaluated.evidence: All 7 headers checked against the 2026-08-19 generalisation (orientation / catalogue / phase-label headers are NOT violations, and 'not every header owes a claim'). Claim-shaped (5 of 7, subject-verb-complement): 'The verifier completes the three-pattern', 'The model has read the field', 'The missing evidence is local', 'The optimum is local, and it moves', 'Every re-feed pass starts a fresh session'. 'Reference and plan' already carries an explicit maintainer accept-note (L73, Antti 2026-08-15: 'not every header owes a claim'). 'One session, plotted' fits the rule's own NOT-violation class 'catalogue entries naming their subject' (parallel to the rule's own listed examples 'The numbers', 'Verification, named') -- it names the chart's subject (one session, plotted as a passage), not a claim slide, and needs no separate accept-note since the compendium states this class as a standing carve-out rather than a per-file exception. No header reads as a mislabeled claim opportunity.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies — three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Read every bullet in all 7 chunks against the three classes (doctrine restatement, self-referential design commentary, aphorism kicker). No class-(b) hit: nothing in the body talks about the curriculum's own pedagogy or design. Closest class-(a)/(c) calls, both held as adding new content rather than pure restatement: chunk 5's closing bullet ('So a playbook stays a candidate until something tests it here...', line 42) echoes chunk 4's 'candidates' but adds the local-test condition that chunk 4 didn't state, setting up chunk 6's promotion mechanism -- progression, not recap. Chunk 6's third bullet closes with 'The local optimum stays ahead, moving when your stack moves' (line 49), which does restate the header, but it is the second half of a bullet whose first half ('a wide first fix that narrows as more experiments land') introduces the promotion mechanism -- not a bare kicker, and not the slide's last bullet (two more follow). The maintainer block already documents one class-(a) cut on this exact file (L77, 2026-08-25: the two sea-passage trailer lines removed 'after the chart already argued it, check_slides.md §16 class a'), confirming this rule has already been swept against this body once; no fresh instance found.
